In this lesson you will learn about two trigger devices.
INTRODUCTIONM
Trigger devices are solid state components which turn ON, or trigger, when its input exceeds a specified value.
Trigger devices are switches...................................
Regular transistors may be used as switches with proper biasing; however, UJTs and SCRs are designed only for switching.
UJTs and SCRs require less circuitry than transistors to perform switching. This saves space and cost.

This is the same as saying that there is a high resistance between the two bases. The resistance is called Interbase Resistance, Rbb.
The emitter forms a PN junction, or diode, between the two bases. It divides Rbb in two.
Rbb1 and Rbb2 form a voltage divider. This places a positive voltage on the cathode of the diode.
The input voltage on the emitter must be larger than +Erbb1 to forward bias the diode and turn ON the UJT.
During the manufacturing process, the placement of the emitter determines the voltage required to overcome Erbb1.

If the value of Rbb1 and Rbb2 are different, a different voltage is required to turn ON the UJT.
Once the UJT is ON, the resistance of Rbb1 drops to near zero.

THE SILICON CONTROL RECTIFIER
The purpose of a silicon control rectifier (SCR) is to switch current On and Off.
DISCUSSION
SCRs turn ON (conduct) when an input current is applied to one of the elements.
The SCR can replace mechanical switches that control large amounts of load current. There are no moving parts to cause arcing or to wear out.
The schematic symbol for SCRs is similar to diodes..............
However, in addition to the anode and cathode, there is a gate....
The anode is the same as a diode's anode.......................
The cathode is the same as a diode's cathode...................
The gate is a line connected to the cathode......................
Touch the cathode on this silicon control rectifier........
You touched the gate. The gate is shown by a line connected to the cathode.
TRY AGAIN!

The name silicon control rectifier is derived from the fact that it is a rectifier (diode) that is controlled by additional semiconductor material.
It is constructed from four semiconductor elements, two N and two P.
The anode is connected to P material as in a diode...............
The cathode is connected to N material as in a diode.............
Only when the anode to cathode is forward biased will current flow, if the gate allows it.
The gate is connected to a thin piece of P material between two pieces of N material. The gate can be as thin as the size of one atom.
It is the action of the gate that makes a SCR different from a normal rectifier diode.

Applying a positive current flow to the gate causes the P material to vanish. Remember, the voltage necessary to cause the current flow must be at least +.7 V.

Removing the gate current once the SCR is ON has no effect. The SCR is latched ON.
The P material gate is eliminated, the two areas of N material stay together and the SCR performs like a forward biased diode.
The only way to restore the P material in the gate is to interrupt anode to cathode current flow.
The only way to restore the P material in the gate is to interrupt cathode to anode current flow.
The purpose of a unijunction transistor (UJT) is to switch voltage.
DISCUSSION
Once the SCR is OFF, it remains OFF until a current is applied to the gate.
UJTs turn ON (conduct) when the input voltage exceeds a specified level.
Transistor reference books list the value as trigger current. For example, a 2N4441 SCR requires 10 mA of gate current to turn it ON.
Even though a small amount of current turns a SCR ON. SCR's output current rating (cathode to anode current) can be as high as 100 A.
Even though a small amount of current turns a SCR ON. SCR's output current rating (anode to cathode current) can be as high as 100 A.
When a SCR is forward biased, what allows anode to cathode current flow?
A large forward bias produces a large anode to cathode current flow when the SCR is ON. The forward bias does not turn a SCR ON.
A large forward bias produces a large cathode to anode current flow when the SCR is ON. The forward bias does not turn a SCR ON.
